customSections.heading: GLP-1/GIP Agonists — Zepbound (Tirzepatide) for OSA with Obesity
customSections.text:
FDA Approval: December 2024 — Tirzepatide (Zepbound) for moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity.

While tirzepatide is primarily approved for OSA (not CSA), it may benefit patients with CSA-OSA overlap syndrome and obesity. The SURMOUNT-OSA trial demonstrated:
- 50.7% mean AHI reduction (vs. 29.3% placebo) in patients not using PAP therapy
- 29.3% mean AHI reduction in patients continuing PAP therapy
- Significant improvements in hypoxic burden, sleep architecture, and quality of life

Prior Authorization Requirements for Zepbound (OSA indication):
- BMI ≥30 kg/m² (or ≥27 with weight-related comorbidity)
- Moderate-to-severe OSA diagnosis (AHI ≥15 events/hour) on PSG
- Not solely for weight loss (OSA indication is separate from obesity indication)
- Step therapy: CPAP trial documentation often required by payers

Reference: Malhotra A, et al. "Tirzepatide for Moderate-to-Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity." N Engl J Med. 2024;391:1421–1432.

# Central Sleep Apnea Authorization Guide
Subtitle: Decision Support
Specialty: Sleep Medicine

## CPT Codes — CSA Evaluation & PAP Therapy

| CPT Code | Description | Auth Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 95810 | Polysomnography (PSG) — in-lab, attended | Often | Required for CSA diagnosis; CAI ≥5 + >50% central events |
| 95811 | PSG with initiation of CPAP/BPAP | Often | PAP titration study |
| 94660 | CPAP initiation and management | Sometimes | First-line PAP therapy |
| E0601 | CPAP device (DME) | Often | AHI ≥5 with CSA diagnosis required |
| E0470 | BPAP device without backup rate | Often | CPAP failure documentation required |
| E0471 | BPAP device with backup rate (BPAP-ST) | Often | Opioid-induced CSA; CPAP/BPAP failure |
| E0601 + modifier | ASV device (adaptive servo-ventilation) | Often | Contraindicated in HFrEF EF <45%; strict criteria |
| 99213–99215 | Office visit — sleep specialist E&M | Rarely | Document CAI, etiology, treatment response |
| 94762 | Nocturnal oximetry | Sometimes | Supplemental O2 titration for CSA-CSR in HF |

## ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Use When |
|---|---|---|
| G47.31 | Primary central sleep apnea | Idiopathic CSA (no identifiable cause) |
| G47.37 | Central sleep apnea in conditions classified elsewhere | CSA due to HF, stroke, opioids — code underlying condition first |
| G47.39 | Other sleep apnea | Treatment-emergent CSA, complex sleep apnea |
| R06.3 | Periodic breathing / Cheyne-Stokes respiration | CSA-CSR pattern on PSG |
| I50.20–I50.9 | Heart failure (HFrEF, HFpEF, unspecified) | Code as primary when CSA-CSR is HF-related |
| F11.20–F11.99 | Opioid use disorder / dependence | Code with G47.37 for opioid-induced CSA |

## Critical Contraindication: ASV in HFrEF

ASV (Adaptive Servo-Ventilation) is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with:
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF): LVEF <45%
- Predominantly central sleep apnea (CSA-CSR pattern)
- NYHA Class II–IV symptoms

Evidence: SERVE-HF trial (Cowie MR, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015;373:1095–1105) demonstrated increased all-cause and cardiovascular mortality with ASV in this population. FDA issued a safety communication in 2015.

AASM 2025 CPG: ASV is conditionally recommended for CSA-CSR in HFpEF (EF ≥45%) only.

## GLP-1/GIP Agonists — Zepbound (Tirzepatide) for OSA with Obesity

FDA Approval: December 2024 — Tirzepatide (Zepbound) for moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity

While tirzepatide is primarily approved for OSA (not CSA), it may benefit patients with CSA-OSA overlap syndrome and obesity. The SURMOUNT-OSA trial demonstrated:
- 50.7% mean AHI reduction (vs. 29.3% placebo) in patients not using PAP therapy
- 29.3% mean AHI reduction in patients continuing PAP therapy
- Significant improvements in hypoxic burden, sleep architecture, and quality of life

Prior Authorization Requirements for Zepbound (OSA indication):
- BMI ≥30 kg/m² (or ≥27 with weight-related comorbidity)
- Moderate-to-severe OSA diagnosis (AHI ≥15 events/hour) on PSG
- Not solely for weight loss (OSA indication is separate from obesity indication)
- Step therapy: CPAP trial documentation often required by payers

Reference: Malhotra A, et al. "Tirzepatide for Moderate-to-Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity." N Engl J Med. 2024;391:1421–1432.

## Documentation Checklist for ASV/BPAP-ST Authorization

- In-lab PSG report: Total AHI, CAI (≥5 events/hour), % central events (>50%)
- CSA etiology clearly documented (idiopathic, HF-related, opioid-induced, treatment-emergent)
- LVEF documented if heart failure present — ASV contraindicated if EF <45%
- CPAP trial: dates, compliance data (≥4 hours/night ≥70% of nights), residual AHI on CPAP
- BPAP trial (if applicable): dates, compliance, residual CAI
- Current opioid medications and doses (MME/day) if opioid-induced CSA
- Cardiology notes if CSA-CSR with HF (NYHA class, most recent echo with EF)
- Physician attestation that ASV is not contraindicated per SERVE-HF criteria

## References

1. Donovan LM, et al. "Treatment of Central Sleep Apnea Syndromes in Adults: An AASM Clinical Practice Guideline." J Clin Sleep Med. 2025.
2. Cowie MR, et al. "Adaptive Servo-Ventilation for Central Sleep Apnea in Systolic Heart Failure." SERVE-HF. N Engl J Med. 2015;373:1095–1105.
3. Malhotra A, et al. "Tirzepatide for Moderate-to-Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity." SURMOUNT-OSA. N Engl J Med. 2024;391:1421–1432.
4. AASM Practice Guidelines: https://aasm.org/clinical-resources/practice-standards/practice-guidelines/
